column1: # Token-count vectors shared by the Rust and Python tests (src/lib.rs, tests/test_token_vectors.py).
# Each line: the expected count, a tab, the text as UTF-8 in hex, a tab, a description.
# The rule: the larger of the number of pieces and a quarter of the characters, rounded up. A piece is a run of
# characters other than whitespace and ASCII symbols, or one ASCII symbol: an ASCII character other than a letter,
# digit, underscore or whitespace. Whitespace is what Python's str.isspace() accepts: Unicode White_Space plus

column3: one space: no pieces, and a quarter of one character rounds up to 1
each ASCII symbol is its own piece
an ASCII symbol between letters splits them
1,000 letters: a quarter of the characters wins
100 words, each followed by a space
U+00AD soft hyphen between letters: not whitespace
U+180E Mongolian vowel separator between letters: not whitespace
U+200B zero width space between letters: not whitespace
U+200C zero width non-joiner between letters: not whitespace
U+200D zero width joiner between letters: not whitespace
U+2060 word joiner between letters: not whitespace
U+FEFF zero width no-break space between letters: not whitespace
a curly apostrophe joins the word
an em dash joins the words
an ellipsis character joins the word
emoji joined by a zero width joiner
an arrow joins the word next to it
mixed ASCII and non-ASCII letters with an underscore and a hyphen
